title: Unnecessary Location Data Collection
description: Backend may collect and transmit more location data than necessary for the app's functionality, violating the minimality principle.
assumptions: Assumes location pings include granular data beyond what is required for core functionality.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: Location History Store may lack adequate access controls, leading to unauthorized disclosure of stored location data.
assumptions: Assumes standard security measures may not be implemented or could be bypassed.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Storing location history may not comply with legal requirements such as GDPR, especially if user consent is not obtained or data retention exceeds necessary periods.
assumptions: Assumes regulatory requirements apply to location data storage.

title: Unauthorized access to zone definitions in data store
description: The Family Account Store contains sensitive location-based zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) that reveal family members' routines and locations. Unauthorized access to DS2 could expose this geolocation data to attackers.
assumptions: Data store has authentication/authorization controls that could be bypassed

title: Interception of zone definition data in transit
description: Zone definitions transmitted from DS2 to P2 could be intercepted during data flow, exposing sensitive location information about family members' regular locations.
assumptions: Data flow may not be encrypted or could be vulnerable to network-level attacks

title: Identification of family members through zone access patterns
description: The Geofencing Engine processes zone definitions that could be used to identify and profile family members based on their location patterns (home, school, social locations).
assumptions: Zone definitions are associated with specific family member identities

title: Linking of family member identities to location data
description: The Geofencing Engine could link zone definitions to specific family member identities, creating a profile that connects individuals to their regular locations and routines.
assumptions: P2 maintains associations between zones and family member identities

title: Family members unaware of location data processing
description: Family members may not be aware that their location-based zone definitions are being read and processed by the Geofencing Engine for tracking purposes.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain geofencing data processing

title: Child Identifiability at Registration
description: Parent provides child's name, date of birth, and school information during profile creation, making the child directly identifiable from the data submitted.
assumptions: Child's personal information is required for account setup and profile creation

title: Parent-Child Linkability
description: Parent's account registration links their identity with the child's profile, creating a persistent association between parent and child that could be exploited for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: System maintains relationship between parent account and child profile

title: Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Child's personal information (name, DOB, school) and geofence zone data transmitted over network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if not properly encrypted.
assumptions: Data transmission occurs over network infrastructure

title: Data Integrity Compromise in Transit
description: Child profile data and geofence definitions could be modified during transmission, potentially leading to incorrect location tracking or profile information.
assumptions: Network transmission is vulnerable to tampering without integrity checks

title: Unawareness of Data Processing Scope
description: Parent may not be fully aware of how the backend processes, stores, or shares child's personal information and geofence data beyond the initial registration.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not clearly communicate all data processing activities

title: Non-compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: Backend processing of child's personal information (name, DOB, school) may not comply with applicable child data protection laws (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding consent, data minimization, and retention.
assumptions: System processes data of minors under applicable jurisdiction
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details

title: Excessive Data Collection in Account Storage
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) may transmit more personal data (e.g., child profile details, geofence zones) to DS2 than strictly necessary for the intended functionality, violating data minimality principles.
assumptions: Assumes the backend does not implement strict data minimization controls before storing in DS2.

title: Non-Compliance with Child Data Protection Regulations
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) may lack required safeguards (e.g., encryption, access controls) for storing sensitive child-related data, risking non-compliance with regulations like COPPA or GDPR.
assumptions: Assumes DS2 does not enforce regulatory-compliant storage practices for child data.

title: Parent-Child Linkability via Request Metadata
description: Parent's request to view child's location includes metadata (e.g., parent ID, timestamp) that could be used to link the parent to the child's location history, enabling profiling or tracking of family relationships.
assumptions: Request includes identifiable parent metadata

title: Child Identifiability in Transit
description: Location data transmitted in the flow may contain child identifiers (e.g., name, device ID) that could be intercepted and used to identify the child.
assumptions: Data includes child identifiers and is transmitted without encryption
uncertainty_note: Assumes no encryption; actual implementation may vary

title: Location Data Disclosure in Transit
description: Unencrypted location data in transit could be intercepted by attackers, leading to unauthorized disclosure of the child's real-time or historical location.
assumptions: Data is transmitted without encryption
uncertainty_note: Assumes no encryption; actual implementation may vary

title: Unauthorized Data Use by Backend
description: Mobile App Backend may process or store location data beyond the scope of the parent's request (e.g., sharing with third parties, retaining data longer than necessary).
assumptions: Backend lacks strict data minimization and access controls

title: Parent Unawareness of Data Processing
description: Parent may not be informed about how their request is processed, including data retention policies or third-party sharing, limiting their ability to make informed decisions.
assumptions: No clear privacy notices or consent mechanisms

title: Non-Compliance with Location Data Regulations
description: Backend may fail to comply with legal requirements (e.g., GDPR, COPPA) regarding location data handling, such as obtaining proper consent or ensuring data security.
assumptions: Backend lacks compliance measures for location data

title: Location data linked to child's identity
description: Backend combines retrieved location history with other data to identify or profile the child beyond intended scope.
assumptions: Backend has access to additional identifying data.

title: Sensitive inferences from location patterns
description: Backend infers sensitive information (e.g., routines, visited locations) from location history data.
assumptions: Location data contains patterns enabling inference.

title: Unauthorized access to location data
description: Backend exposes location history to unauthorized parties due to weak access controls.
assumptions: Access controls on backend are insufficient.

title: Location data altered in transit
description: Location history data is modified during transfer between DS1 and P1.
assumptions: Data in transit lacks integrity protections.
uncertainty_note: Internal network may have encryption, but not guaranteed.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child's location to secondary guardian

assumptions: Secondary guardian access requires explicit authorization from primary guardian

title: Location data interception during transmission

title: Secondary guardian sharing location data beyond intended scope

title: Primary guardian unaware of secondary guardian location access

title: Secondary guardian unaware of data handling obligations

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations

title: Lack of user awareness about data sharing

title: Data misuse beyond agreed purpose

title: Linking data across sources

assumptions: EE4 has access to additional user data from other sources.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations

title: Attributable check-in/SOS action
description: The child's manual check-in or SOS message creates evidence that can be attributed to them, potentially holding them accountable for their location and actions at a specific time.
assumptions: The system logs or records the child's check-in/SOS actions

title: Location data interception in transit

assumptions: Data is transmitted over potentially insecure network channels
